overview: B&M is a leading European variety discount retailer operating around 1,300 stores across three fascias: B&M UK (general merchandise and FMCG discount stores), Heron Foods/B&M Express (UK convenience food discount), and B&M France (a growing multi-year expansion opportunity). The group sells a targeted range of best-selling FMCG and General Merchandise products at everyday low prices, sourced directly and run through a low-cost, low-capital-intensity operating model. It is listed on the LSE (FTSE 250), redomiciled its parent company from Luxembourg to Jersey in February 2026, and reports on a 52/53-week year ending late March.

business_model.summary: B&M is an Everyday Low Price (EDLP) / Everyday Low Cost (EDLC) variety discount retailer. It directly sources FMCG (groceries, health & beauty, household) and General Merchandise (seasonal/garden, toys, home, DIY) and sells through a low-cost, no-frills store estate with fast payback new-store economics. Growth comes from a mix of like-for-like sales growth and disciplined new store rollout, funded mainly from internally generated cash flow.

revenue_streams.name: Heron Foods / B&M Express (discount food convenience)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market value/discount shopper, with some wholesale (e.g. Centz Retail Holdings associate in Ireland)
business_model.geographic_mix: UK ~90% of group revenue (B&M UK + Heron/B&M Express), France ~10% and growing (FY26: B&M UK £4,615m, B&M France £616m, Heron Foods £544m of £5,775m total)

main_competitors: supermarkets (Tesco, Asda, Sainsbury's) moving into value ranges
competitive_position.market_position: One of the UK's two largest variety/general-merchandise discounters alongside privately-held Home Bargains; both have taken share from Poundland and traditional retailers over 2019-2024 (GlobalData estimates Home Bargains +7.2ppts and B&M +6.2ppts of UK discount share vs Poundland -2.3ppts over that period). B&M France is a smaller, fast-growing challenger position in Continental Europe.

moat_factors.description: Direct sourcing, lean store format, low capital intensity and fast new-store payback support industry-leading margins and allow price leadership even after recent margin erosion
Close to 1,300 stores and ~£5.8bn revenue give meaningful purchasing scale, reinforced by a new c.700,000 sq ft Ellesmere Port import/automation hub targeting 70% of network container volume
Long-established reputation for amazing value and treasure-hunt General Merchandise, though recent execution drift (pricing, availability, range complexity) has weakened this versus Home Bargains
Estate of retail parks, high streets and town centres gives broad geographic reach, though lacks e-commerce or loyalty-programme moat that competitors increasingly build

weaknesses: Lost competitive ground to privately-held Home Bargains, widely viewed as currently executing better in the same segment
Heron Foods convenience food business has structurally weaker margins and has been in LFL decline for two years
No material e-commerce, loyalty programme, or private-label infrastructure versus increasingly sophisticated rivals and supermarkets
Execution drift over FY25/FY26 (pricing, promotions, ranging, on-shelf availability) show the model is not self-sustaining without active management discipline
Heavily reliant on UK consumer discretionary and FMCG spend with limited pricing power insulation from input-cost/regulatory cost inflation

growth_drivers: 'Back to B&M Basics' turnaround plan (price, promotions, ranges, on-shelf availability) aimed at restoring sustainable UK like-for-like growth; showing early traction (B&M UK LFL +3.2% in Q2 FY27 after declines in FY26)

B&M France expansion - smaller store base (156 stores vs ~799 in UK) with strong like-for-like growth (+5.9% H1 FY27) and considered a multi-year, higher-growth opportunity with similar economics to the UK
UK store estate growth toward a long-term target of ~1,200 B&M stores (from 799), plus continued Heron Foods/B&M Express rollout, moderated near-term to fund store re-lays/refits
Phase 2 'B&M 2.0' store concept (new format trialled in Wigan, wider aisles, self-checkout, data-driven store clustering) intended to boost productivity of the existing UK estate
Phase 3 longer-term optionality: private label, e-commerce, and loyalty programmes under consideration (not yet committed)
Ellesmere Port automated import/distribution centre expected to drive structural cost-per-case efficiency and support further UK store growth
Capital allocation flexibility post-Jersey redomicile (completed Feb 2026), enabling potential future share buybacks as leverage and cash generation allow

business.risk: Intensifying competition from Home Bargains and other discounters
business.description: Home Bargains has been gaining share and is viewed by commentators as currently out-executing B&M in the same core segment
Two consecutive years of LFL decline and margin compression; management is applying a similar turnaround playbook as B&M UK but success is unproven

'Back to B&M Basics' is only partway through its targeted 12-18 month delivery window; new CEO (Tjeerd Jegen, from June 2025) and reshuffled leadership team still being bedded in, with a new permanent CFO (Atheeq Akbar) not starting until January/February 2027

business.risk: Customer/product obsolescence risk in General Merchandise
business.description: Reliance on seasonal, discretionary categories (garden, toys, Christmas) makes revenue sensitive to weather and consumer discretionary trends

financial.description: Net debt (pre-IFRS 16) to adjusted EBITDA of 1.43x at FY26 (within 1.0x-1.5x target) but higher-coupon £250m bond issued Nov 2024 (6.5% vs prior 3.625%) raised finance costs; including IFRS 16 leases, leverage is c.2.9x
Ordinary dividend and special dividends have been reduced over FY25-FY26 as profits fell; policy targets 40-50% of adjusted post-IFRS16 earnings, which fluctuates with profitability
Growing B&M France business creates GBP/EUR translation exposure as France becomes a larger share of group revenue and profit

regulatory.description: National Minimum Wage increases, higher Employer National Insurance contributions, and the new Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) levy materially increased FY26 operating costs and are expected to recur

regulatory.risk: Compliance and regulatory risk flagged as increasing
regulatory.description: FY26 annual report specifically flagged increased risk exposure in regulation & compliance and is investing in systems/controls to bring this back within tolerance

macro.description: Business proposition benefits from value-seeking behavior in a cost-of-living squeeze, but weak real wage growth or recession could also pressure discretionary General Merchandise spend

FY26 annual report cites the Middle East conflict and its effect on international freight, domestic distribution and energy costs as an ongoing, significant (though not currently material) cost pressure
Garden/outdoor General Merchandise sales in Q1 are highly weather-dependent, as demonstrated by weak Q1 FY27 comparisons against an unusually warm/dry April 2025

macro_factors.industry_outlook: UK and European variety/general-merchandise discount retail is viewed as a structurally growing channel as consumers continue trading down, though the sector has recently shown signs of maturing competitive intensity (Poundland's troubles, B&M and Home Bargains both reporting slower growth versus the 2020-2023 period)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - value retail is relatively defensive in downturns (trading-down benefit) but General Merchandise/seasonal categories carry discretionary-spend and weather sensitivity
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - leveraged balance sheet (freehold-light, lease-heavy model) and bond refinancing at higher coupons increase sensitivity to UK rate levels
key_input_costs: UK National Minimum Wage / National Insurance

recent_developments.event: FY27 interim results (26 weeks to 26 Sept 2026): Group revenue +3.6% to £2,848m, adjusted EBITDA (pre-IFRS16) +6.0% to £203m, adjusted PBT +16.6% to £121m; B&M UK LFL turned positive (+0.4% H1, +3.2% in Q2) for the first time in several periods; management introduced FY27 guidance of adjusted EBITDA £450-500m and adjusted PBT £280-330m
Launched new 'B&M 2.0' concept store format in Wigan (wider aisles, self-checkout, store clustering by customer profile), later named IGD's Store of the Month for November 2026

Q1 FY27 trading statement: Group revenue +2.0%; B&M UK LFL sales declined -2.3% (weak garden/outdoor start vs strong prior-year comparative), while B&M France (+5.3% LFL) and Heron Foods (+2.6% LFL) both grew
Announced incoming permanent CFO Atheeq Akbar (ex-ASDA/Morrisons/Tesco), to start February 2027; Peter Waterhouse continuing as Interim CFO following Mike Schmidt's departure

FY26 annual results (year to 28 March 2026): Group revenue +3.6% to £5.8bn but adjusted EBITDA -25.9% to £459m and statutory PBT -47.3% to £227m, reflecting UK margin erosion, cost inflation (NMW, NI, EPR levy) and a £36m store/lease impairment charge; dividend reduced
Completed redomicile of parent company from Luxembourg to Jersey, simplifying governance and increasing flexibility for future capital returns (e.g., buybacks)
New Group Trading Director (Simon Hathway, ex-Action) and Group People Director (Jennifer Lawrence, ex-Card Factory) joined the Executive team as part of leadership strengthening

Launched the 'Back to B&M Basics' turnaround plan (price, promotions, ranges, on-shelf availability) following a profit warning and weak H1 FY26 trading, with an explicit 12-18 month timeframe to restore UK LFL growth

Tjeerd Jegen (former Action/European discount retail executive) became CEO, succeeding Alex Russo, who had retired following a string of profit warnings and the share price falling to a multi-year low

items.vs_prior: new guidance (first full-year FY27 guide); versus FY26 actual of £459m
items.notes: Introduced alongside H1 results after positive early Golden Quarter trading; midpoint implies modest recovery/stabilisation versus FY26

items.vs_prior: new guidance; versus FY26 actual of £284m
items.notes: Reflects expectation of improving UK General Merchandise category margin and continued LFL recovery in H2
Reduced from previously guided 25-35 gross as capital is redirected to store re-lays/refits (Phase 2 format investment); expected to revert to 25-35 gross in FY28
Management reiterates confidence B&M UK can return to double-digit EBITDA margins over the medium term as LFL growth and category margin recover; not a near-term FY27 target
FY26 effective rate was 26% and management expects this to continue into FY27

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Tjeerd Jegen said 'Back to B&M Basics is starting to deliver,' citing the Q2 FY27 return to UK LFL growth (+3.2%) and improving General Merchandise category margin as validation of the turnaround plan, while flagging a slower pace of new UK store openings in FY27 to fund store re-lays/refits (Phase 2) ahead of accelerating growth (Phase 3, including possible private label, e-commerce and loyalty investments). Management described early Golden Quarter (H2) trading as positive across all three businesses with continued LFL growth in both FMCG and General Merchandise at B&M UK.

bull_case: Early, tangible evidence the 'Back to B&M Basics' turnaround is working: UK LFL sales returned to growth (+3.2% in Q2 FY27) after a prolonged period of decline, with General Merchandise margin recovering
B&M France offers a long, underpenetrated growth runway (156 stores vs ~799 in UK) with consistently strong double-digit revenue growth and improving LFL momentum (+5.9% H1 FY27)
Highly cash-generative, low-capital-intensity business model with strong free cash flow (£321m FY26, up YoY) even through the profit downturn, supporting deleveraging and future capital returns
New CEO and refreshed leadership team (CFO, Trading Director, People Director, Heron MD) bring external discount-retail expertise and have moved quickly to diagnose and address execution problems
Shares have de-rated heavily from 2024 highs, meaning a successful turnaround could offer significant re-rating upside versus currently depressed sell-side price targets
bear_case: Home Bargains continues to out-execute B&M in the same core discount segment, raising doubts about whether 'Back to Basics' can fully close the competitive gap rather than just stabilise the business
Heron Foods remains in LFL decline with weak margins and is only now beginning a turnaround effort, adding execution risk on a second front
Structural UK cost inflation (National Minimum Wage, Employer NI, EPR levy) is recurring and could continue to outpace any margin recovery, capping profitability improvement
Turnaround is still in early stages (announced October 2025, 12-18 month horizon) with a new, not-yet-arrived permanent CFO; meaningful execution risk remains before the plan is proven sustainable
Dividend has already been cut materially and leverage (c.2.9x including leases) constrains the pace of further capital returns or buybacks while the business stabilises
